u71zqa: "Not yet" answer question completed; The following clause "but I am planning to finish it tonight" – "plan + to V", the adverb of time "tonight" comes at the end of the sentence.
6no80u: Present continuous passive: "is being + V3" (being edited). "by a technician" (by a technician) comes after a passive verb.
1ycjvb2: Advice "You should + V" (you should…). The prepositional phrase "on the corner" comes immediately after the noun it modifies ("the café"); The reason clause "because it is quieter" is placed at the end of the sentence.

efm7sk: Basic order S + modal + V + O: "you can download it". "the department website" is a compound noun (faculty website).
bss1lr: "much" comparative emphasis: "much more interesting than I expected" (much more interesting than I thought).
13h5u8g: "I wonder + who + will + V" – question nested in a declarative sentence, ending with a period. "who" as the subject should come right before "will teach".
1ux4231: Structure "be (not) worth + V-ing" (worth/not worth doing): "it is not worth waiting for the bus".
1ttyuhl: Order S + be + adj: "it is open"; two opposing time clusters connected by "but not": "on Saturday but not on Sunday".
kf74yg: Structure "find + O + adj + to V" (how to see something): "found her talk easy to follow"; The adverb "surprisingly" comes before the adjective "easy" to modify.
u39h0a: Polite cage question: "Could you tell me + which building + S + V". In a nested clause that is NOT inverted: "which building it is in", the preposition "in" comes last.
rfp4jm: Reported sentence: "S + said + that + clause". "be due" = due; The adverb of time "next Friday" comes at the end of the sentence.
ibgzof: Polite refusal: "I would love to, but…". Present perfect "I have already promised"; "already" stands between "have" and V3; "promise + to V".
ndnht0: Answer "No" then add: "but I have heard that it is amazing" – present perfect "have heard" + clause "that".
1orkyb9: Long subject with relative clause: "The one that the professor recommended" + "is the most useful". "the one" instead of "the book".
1v2p58w: Present perfect passive "has been + V3" (closed). "because of + noun" (because) – do not use "because" before a noun phrase.
lzn5dz: "try + to V" (try to do something); The frequency phrase "at least three times a week" (at least three times a week) comes at the end of the sentence.
1at731m: Superlative + present perfect with "ever": "the most interesting trip I have ever taken" (the most exciting trip I've ever been on); Reduced relative clauses omit "that".
1jbc1ww: Basic sentence order S + V + place + go with someone: "I studied in the library with two friends"; The phrase "from my class" modifies "two friends" so it comes right after.
1y5c2uk: Structure "so + adj + that + clause" (so … that): "so relaxing that I forgot about my homework"; "forget about" = forgot.
19nnpd: Polite cage question: "Could you tell me + where + S + V". In a nested clause DO NOT invert: "where the nearest post office is" (not "where is the…").
1o7akqk: "realize that + clause" (realize that); comparative "more interested in A than in B" – preposition "in" repeats on both sides.
tmpk3l: Agree with conditions: "Sure, as long as + clause" (as long as); "give them back" – pronoun "them" stands between the verb and the particle "back".
1nba9yb: Structure "tell + O + to V" (tell someone to do something): "told me to narrow it down"; "narrow down" = narrow; "a little more" (a little more) comes last.
ksn1v7: "be going to + V" expresses intention; The relative clause "that my aunt manages" modifies "a museum" (the museum that my aunt manages).

195hk8g: Past passive S + was + past participle: "the bus was delayed"; "because of + noun phrase" gives the reason and comes after: "because of the heavy snow".
5j5owz: Negative present perfect "haven't + past participle"; the phrase "make up my mind" = decide; "yet" goes at the end of a negative sentence.
jpyxel: S + be + place: "it's on the third floor"; the extra location phrase "next to the library entrance" comes after it.
139nm88: Reported command: tell + someone + to + verb → "she told us to finish the first draft"; the deadline "by Friday" goes at the end.
15zd170: The answer uses a clause after "I think": "I think it opens at seven thirty" – the subject "it" is singular, so "opens" takes -s; "at" + a clock time.
wdd2g4: Comparative with an intensifier: "much + quieter + than"; "the one (that) I lived in last year" is a relative clause with the pronoun left out.
1yrl635: A Wh- question with "would you like + someone + to + verb": "where would you like me to put them?"
1datc8t: Comparative "more interesting than"; the past perfect "I had expected" describes what the speaker thought BEFORE the lecture.
bnp9a: The pattern "one of + the + superlative + plural noun": "one of the best engineering programs"; the place "in the country" goes at the end.
19rfj5z: Gentle advice with "might want to + verb" (maybe you should…): "you might want to bring your notes from last week".
fpbp82: S + V + O: "I found it"; then the place "in a journal", and the relative clause "that my professor recommended" describes "a journal", so it must come straight after it.
7r00u9: tell + someone + that + clause: "nobody told me that…"; past perfect passive "it had been moved" (the meeting was moved BEFORE that time); "move to + the new time".
kzmbho: Present perfect continuous "have been + V-ing" for an action that continues up to now; "since + a point in time or a past clause": "since I was ten".
1bozzfb: An indirect question after "I'm not sure": whether + S + V in normal statement order ("whether it opens", not the inverted "does it open"); "on weekends" goes at the end.
1wekef9: suggest + that + S + base verb (subjunctive): "that I take", not "took" or "to take".
1rqo0o4: A Wh- question with "which + noun": "which program" + the auxiliary moved before the subject, "are you using"; the purpose phrase "to open it" goes at the end.
1qqy06m: The pronoun "the one" + the prepositional phrase "with a balcony"; the relative clause "that faces the park" describes "a balcony" – the subject is singular, so "faces" takes -s.
119v1rx: Modal verb "can + base verb": "you can keep them"; "until + a point in time" goes at the end: "until the end of the week".
6do5u6: The adverb "still" comes before the main verb "have"; the pattern "have + noun + left + to + verb" = still have … to do: "two chapters left to read".
oqzkpl: Present continuous "are preparing" for something happening now; "prepare for + an exam"; the time phrase "next week" describes "the final exams", so it goes at the end.
1n138cd: Reported speech with the tense moved back: "will" → "would" after "told me that"; "hear from someone" = get news from someone; "within two weeks" goes at the end.
15vozyk: The instruction "make sure (that) + S + V": "make sure you bring" (not "to bring"); "bring something with you" = carry it with you, and "with you" goes at the end.
8u3dvr: Past simple "closed" is used with "ago"; "about ten minutes ago" – "about" comes before the number.
1ux20as: The clause after "we think" keeps statement word order; negative past passive "were not stored" (the samples were not kept properly); "at the right temperature" goes at the end.
1rxjt1k: The possessive relative clause "whose work" describes "researchers"; the past perfect "I had cited" – the citing happened BEFORE the meeting.
109fdti: An indirect question "Do you know if + S + V" – after "if", keep statement order: "it has been moved" (present perfect passive), not the inverted "has it been".
